explicit_non_goals: No invented operation, quantity, bound, target, reset scope, service mapping, audit field or idempotency rule.
No runtime, Telegram or production persistence wiring.

refined_contract.contract: Give, Reset and Set are application commands. Telegram handlers and DEV compatibility helpers are adapters, not the V2 invariant-owning boundary.
The Stage 21.15.1 authorization decision must succeed before target lookup, repository mutation, notification or audit append. Disabled or unauthorized paths produce no observable side effect.
Each operation invokes a typed application-service port and repository/Unit-of-Work abstraction. V1 direct SQL is behavioral evidence only and is not an authorized V2 bypass.
Validation, mutation and required audit/idempotency receipt are one atomic application transaction. Any mandatory failure rolls back the complete operation.
Each command declares one canonical target kind: account, user, character, item definition or inventory instance. Identifiers are not interchangeable and must be resolved before mutation.

Give operations validate the authoritative item/currency/resource identity and quantity, then use the canonical service that preserves binding, namespace, stack, capacity, wallet and ledger invariants evidenced by V1.

Reset uses an explicit field/scope policy. Character-level data may be reset only where V1 proves it; account-level wallets, entitlements, audit ledgers and other preserved data must not be deleted by implication.
Set operations validate exact V1 bounds and derive dependent state through canonical domain/application services. Raw field assignment cannot bypass level, EXP, stats, wallet or inventory invariants.
Where V1 proves durable audit or idempotency, V2 preserves it within the transaction. A universal receipt is not invented for operations lacking evidence; parity resolution must decide per command.
The application service returns a deterministic result. External notification occurs only after commit and is not part of the domain mutation transaction.
Any Stage 21.15.2c domain contract is implemented in the flat module rom_v2/domain/dev_data_operations.py; rom_v2/domain/dev_data_operations/ is prohibited.

superseded_interpretations: A handler or compatibility helper is not the V2 application-service boundary.
V1 direct SQL is not automatically authorized for V2.
User, account, character, item definition and inventory instance IDs are not interchangeable.
Reset does not imply deletion of account-level wallets, entitlements or audit data.
Set does not imply raw assignment without dependent invariant recalculation.
Keyword matches outside authoritative owners do not define operation policy.

unresolved_for_parity.reason: Exact effective Give/Reset/Set commands must be resolved after Python shadowing and registration order.
Canonical target kind and lookup semantics must be resolved per operation.
Exact item/currency/resource identities, quantities, caps, binding and capacity behavior require V1 owner resolution.
Exact reset/delete/preserve fields and account-vs-character boundaries require parity resolution.
Exact bounds and dependent recalculation behavior for level, EXP, gold and other setters require parity resolution.
Each operation must map to an existing V2 service/repository or an explicitly authorized port without direct SQL.
Durable audit and idempotency requirements are not proven uniform across all operations.
Exact notification and history/domain-event behavior must be resolved per operation.
